title: TTMC: Brain-Inspired Test-Time Memory Calibration with Orthogonal Projection for Online Continual Learning

problem.claim: Online continual learning methods based on parameter-efficient fine-tuning freeze model parameters after training and therefore do not adapt to covariate shift in non-stationary test streams.

gap.claim: Analytic learning approaches can suffer geometric distortion and feature aliasing because they rely on Gaussian random projection in finite dimensions.

contributions.claim: TTMC is a gradient-free analytic framework that treats memory as a dynamic associative pool.
TTMC fuses second-order statistics from an unlabelled test stream into accumulated long-term memory through a closed-form transductive calibration mechanism.
The work argues that Isometric Orthogonal Projections are necessary for geometric stability, preserving energy and minimizing feature interference.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present Test-Time Memory Calibration as a novel gradient-free analytic framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that TTMC establishes a new state-of-the-art across diverse benchmarks.
The authors report that the method requires zero backward passes and has negligible computational overhead.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing online continual learning methods freeze parameters and fail to adapt to covariate shift in non-stationary test streams.
Gaussian random projections introduce geometric distortion and feature aliasing in finite-dimensional analytic learning.
TTMC introduces dynamic test-time memory calibration using an associative memory view and closed-form fusion of test-stream statistics.
Isometric orthogonal projections are proposed as the geometrically stable projection mechanism.
The authors report state-of-the-art performance with zero backward passes and negligible computational overhead.

source_observation.claim: The proposed projection mechanism is intended to conserve energy and reduce feature interference.

interpretation.claim: Projection geometry may be a central stability factor when adapting representations online.

application.claim: When designing finite-dimensional analytic online learning systems, evaluate orthogonal projections as an alternative to Gaussian random projections.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide the proof details or conditions under which the claimed necessity holds.
